elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1: "each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the event" — the cap runs to both Parties symmetrically, and no residual unlimited-Customer-liability language remains.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 21.1 as amended reads "Fees actually paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the event" — it uses "actually paid" rather than "paid or payable" and contains no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.2 (retained): "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.1 now opens "Except for Excluded Claims", and 21.3 defines Excluded Claims to include "a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations"; the conflicting "without exception" tail has been removed.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims (21.3) expressly covers "data-protection, or security obligations", and 21.1 is now subject to Excluded Claims.
21.3 includes "its indemnification obligations" within Excluded Claims, which 21.1 now carves out of the cap.
21.3: Excluded Claims include "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud"; 21.1 excepts Excluded Claims from the cap.
21.3 lists "wilful misconduct" among Excluded Claims, now carved out of the 21.1 cap.
21.3 lists "fraud" among Excluded Claims, now carved out of the 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" is an Excluded Claim, excepted from 21.1.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 21.3 only says "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages". "Fees" is defined in 1.5 to exclude taxes, reimbursable expenses, interest and any one-time implementation charge, and the carve-out is further narrowed to undisputed amounts for conforming Services, so it does not cover Customer's payment obligations as a whole.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: 21.1 as rendered is mutual ("each Party's"), sets a twelve (12) months' Fees basis, and is now expressly "Except for Excluded Claims", with 21.3 defining Excluded Claims to include indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Preferred is not reached for two reasons the drafter should note (correctly disclaimed in the rationale/comment): (i) 21.1 must read "the greater of (a) Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000" — "actually paid" and the absent USD 1,000,000 floor both fail element 2; (ii) the payment carve-out in 21.3 is limited to "undisputed Fees for conforming Services", and because "Fees" (s.1.5) excludes taxes, reimbursable expenses, interest and implementation charges, it does not exempt Customer's payment obligations generally.

Minimality holds: the edit changes only the cap basis (one month to twelve months), inserts the "Except for Excluded Claims" lead-in, and deletes "without exception" — that deletion is necessary because the retained words would directly contradict the new Excluded Claims exception. No survival tails, expense language, extra damages categories or boilerplate were added, and favourable retained language in 21.2 and 21.3 (direct-damages characterisation, payment carve-out) is untouched.

Intent is preserved: 21.2 already referenced Excluded Claims, so the forward reference in 21.1 to the definition in 21.3 creates no dangling term or undefined trigger, and no unrelated remedy, timing or commercial mechanic is contradicted.
